title: Google Sheets API: How to Use It (2026 Guide)
summary: The google sheets api is free for Google Cloud projects within quotas.
body_markdown:
## Google Sheets API access, scope and cost


### What the Sheets API is and what it can do


It's a programmatic interface to spreadsheets: you read and write cell values, append rows, format ranges, manage tabs, and bundle many edits into one batch request.


The ceiling's the same whether you call it from your own code or through[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , whose Google Sheets integration sits in an MIT-licensed open source repository and calls the same API.


Treat the last row as a design constraint, because a sheet you append to daily has an end date you can calculate. The table below lists what Google's documentation states on endpoint, cost, access, capabilities and cell limit, and which page says it.


Item What Google's docs state Source page


Endpoint REST API at sheets.googleapis.com Google Sheets API reference


Cost No charge for API use; requests are governed by quotas Sheets API usage limits


Access method Enable the API in a Google Cloud project; authorize with OAuth 2.0 or a service account Sheets API overview


Capabilities Read, write, format and batch-update spreadsheet data Sheets API reference


Cell limit 20 million cells per spreadsheet Google Sheets Help, spreadsheet size limits


*Prices and plan limits checked against[docs.claude.com](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/overview) and[claude.com](https://claude.com/pricing) and[openai.com](https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing) and[gemini.google](https://gemini.google/subscriptions) on November 19, 2026.*


*Checked 19 November 2026.* Nothing in this table asks for a billing plan, so the remaining question is how to switch the API on.


You create or choose a project in the Google Cloud console and enable the Google Sheets API for it. Then create credentials: an OAuth client if people sign in, or a service account if a server acts alone.


The project is the unit Google counts quota against, so every script sharing one project shares one allowance.


Nobody sends you a bill for a request. Google's usage-limits page describes quotas, not a price list, so the practical risk is throttling.


The bill you can avoid worrying about is the API's; the failure you should plan for is hitting a quota and needing retries.

### Which Google account or Workspace plan you need


Start with a free Google account; it's enough. Workspace is optional, and only worth it for admin controls or shared domains.


Per[Justin McKelvey's pricing breakdown](https://justinmckelvey.com/blog/google-workspace-pricing) , Business Starter is $7 per user per month, which is the cheapest step if you want a managed domain, so professional email doesn't require a large budget.

According to Justin McKelvey, Business Standard is $14, double that, and Business Plus is $22, over three times Starter.


Pay for them only for what they add outside the API, because none of those upgrades unlocks a different Sheets API.
